spans.s:
1. Iṭa.--This word occurs twice in the Atharvaveda. in the first passage it seems to denote a bulrush of the sort that dies in a year; in the second it refers to the reed work of the house.
Foot notes vi. 14, 3. Cf. iv. 19, 1; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 464.
ix. 3, 18. Cf. Pischel, Zeitschrift der Deutschen Morgenlāndischen Gesellschaft, 35, 718.

2. Iṭa appears as a ṛṣi and a protégé of indra in one hymn of the Rigveda. Roth, however, thinks that the word is really part of a verb (iṭ) meaning ‘to err, wander’ (cp. aṭ), and that the name is a mere misunderstanding. It is already so regarded in the Anukramaṇī, but not apparently in the Bṛhaddevatā.
Foot notes x. 171, 1.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v.
viii. 73. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 133.

Iṭant Kāvya is the name of a sage, contemporary with keśin dārbhya, in the Kauṣitaki brāhmaṇa. He is also mentioned as Iḍhant in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes vii. 4. Cf. Weber, Indische Studien, 1, 293; 2, 308.
xiv. 9, 16.
